tagline: A wholly-owned insurance subsidiary of Equinor ASA providing captive insurance and risk management services to the Equinor group
hero_kpi_rationale: Equins' primary earnings source stems from financial management of its assets, not insurance premiums.

kpis.name: Net Investment Gains
kpis.explanation: Profit or loss realized on financial investments managed by the insurance subsidiary.
kpis.description: In 2023, Equins recorded net investment gains of USD 217 million, compared to a loss in 2022 (-4.07%).
kpis.signal: Return to profitability after a 2022 loss, with a return of 8.26% in 2023

kpis.name: Total Financial Assets
kpis.explanation: Total value of financial assets held by the insurance subsidiary at year-end.
kpis.description: Financial assets reached USD 3,106.6 million at end of 2023, compared to USD 2,492.3 million in 2022.
kpis.signal: Significant growth in assets under management

kpis.name: Gross Insurance Premiums
kpis.explanation: Total amount of insurance premiums collected, before reinsurance cost deductions.
kpis.description: Gross premiums increased from USD 176.5 million in 2022 to USD 264 million in 2023.
kpis.signal: Strong increase in gross premiums in 2023

kpis.name: Claims Costs
kpis.explanation: Amount of claim payments supported directly by the insurance company.
kpis.description: Own claims costs declined from USD 95.3 million in 2022 to USD 86.8 million in 2023.

kpis.name: Solvency Ratio
kpis.explanation: Ratio of available capital to required capital under the Solvency II regulatory framework.
kpis.description: The solvency ratio improved from 189% in 2022 to 269% in 2023, well above the regulatory threshold.
kpis.signal: Major improvement in financial strength and capacity to support risks

kpis.name: Total Workforce
kpis.explanation: Total number of full-time employees in the company.
kpis.description: The company had 4 full-time employees at end of 2023, evenly split between men and women (2 men, 2 women).
kpis.signal: Very lean structure with equal gender balance

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 7.1272 NOK in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 4.791 billion NOK in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout ratio: Dividends paid / Net income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 95.0% in the latest year.

risks.title: Complete concentration on Equinor group operations
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned as a concentration risk: 'non-life insurance which is entirely linked to the Equinor group's operations'. Direct language with no mitigation. Stable structural trend. Client concentration category is critical for a captive insurer.

risks.title: Catastrophic claims risk linked to oil and gas operations
risks.score_rationale: The filing emphasizes that 'both the frequency of claims and the claims amount can vary widely' due to the nature of oil and gas operations. Historical data shows gross claims reaching USD 612 million in 2019. Strong language, volatile trend confirmed over 5 years.

risks.title: Critical dependence on external reinsurance program
risks.score_rationale: The filing describes structural reliance on non-proportional reinsurance and Everen Insurance Limited to cover claims up to USD 240 million per event. Failure of a key reinsurer is an explicitly managed risk via minimum rating requirements. Stable trend but significant exposure.

risks.title: Joint liability within the Everen mutual structure
risks.score_rationale: The filing explicitly states that 'Equinor Insurance AS is responsible for a share of any losses that may arise in connection with Everen's business'. This mutual liability risk is specific to the captive/mutual structure. Clear language, potentially material risk depending on other members' claims.

risks.title: Actuarial uncertainty on IBNR and IBNER reserves
risks.score_rationale: The filing devotes several paragraphs to reserve provisioning uncertainties (RBNS, IBNR, IBNER) and acknowledges that 'the final claim amounts will differ from the prior and original claim amount'. Development data shows massive revisions (e.g., 2019: USD 51 million to USD 612 million). Structural trend inherent to the business.

risks.title: Tax dispute on deductibility of intra-group premiums
risks.score_rationale: The filing mentions a dispute with the Norwegian Oil Tax Office over the deductibility of premiums paid by Equinor ASA and Equinor Energy AS to the captive. Although partially resolved, a tax claim of USD 22.9 million remains outstanding as of 31 December 2023. Trend improving but residual risk.

risks.title: Solvency II regulatory and capital requirements risk
risks.score_rationale: The filing references capital calculations under the Solvency II standard model (EIOPA) for equity, interest rate and currency risks. Stress tests show significant value reductions (e.g., Type 1 equities: -39%). EIOPA regulation is constraining and evolving. Stable trend with risk of tightening.

risks.title: Geopolitical exposure through international insured operations
risks.score_rationale: The geographic distribution table of reserves covers Norway, USA, UK, Canada, Brazil, Russia and Azerbaijan. The Russian reserve was reduced to zero in 2023 (vs. USD 619 thousand in 2022), reflecting post-conflict disengagement. Evolving trend with residual risk in unstable zones.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence, technological innovation or AI-related initiatives in the annual report. The business is centered on traditional insurance risk management and financial portfolio management.
evidence: No reference to AI or emerging technologies
Business described as purely insurance and financial in nature
Absence of R&D or technological innovation
